title: How did a dodo become the subject of a Mughal painting?
short: A Mughal bird study apparently depicts a dodo. Can the bird that served as its model be traced from Mauritius to India?
matters: A connection between the study and a documented bird would show how a living animal moved from Mauritius into a South Asian world of trade, gifts and painting.
stuck: Peter Mundy recalled seeing two living dodos in Surat. The album catalogue dates the bird study to about 1615, attributes it to Manṣūr, and describes the assembled page as a later collage. No surviving record connects a particular bird to the artist.
solved: A dated shipping or gift record should link a landing in India to a person or place connected with the painter, with a chronology that fits the study.
approach: Trace animals through original cargo lists, letters and gifts. Use the published 1615 Wapen van Amsterdam journal as a starting point and test the attribution and dating independently.
